airline_fuel_cost.name: Airline fuel-cost shock
airline_fuel_cost.summary: What a change in crude oil, jet fuel and the exchange rate does to an airline's fuel bill and operating profit, month by month, with hedging and fare pass-through.
airline_fuel_cost.description: A deterministic, monthly model of one airline. The baseline fuel bill is annual consumption × the benchmark jet fuel price × the exchange rate. Scenario changes to crude oil (propagated to jet fuel along a validated knowledge-graph relationship), to jet fuel directly and to the exchange rate change the monthly bill. Hedges fix the dollar price of part of the fuel for a number of months; fares recover a share of the change after a lag. Everything else stays at its baseline. Version 1.1.0 adds the timing of the changes: a start month and a duration.

inputs.label: Crude oil price change
inputs.description: Change in the Brent crude oil price, in percent (30 means +30 %). It takes effect in the start month and lasts for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless a duration is set). It reaches jet fuel only through the knowledge-graph relationship 'Brent crude influences jet fuel' (rule T1).
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Additional jet fuel price change
inputs.description: A change in the jet fuel price beyond what crude oil explains (for example a wider refining margin), in percent. It takes effect in the start month and lasts for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless a duration is set).
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Exchange-rate change
inputs.description: Change in the price of one US dollar in the reporting currency, in percent. Positive means the reporting currency weakens (more rupees per dollar), which raises the cost of dollar-priced fuel. It takes effect in the start month and lasts for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless a duration is set).
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Baseline jet fuel price
inputs.description: The benchmark jet fuel price the airline's fuel is priced from, in US dollars per unit of volume. RUMIN holds no jet fuel prices: enter the benchmark and the date you rely on.

inputs.label: Baseline exchange rate
inputs.description: Units of the reporting currency per US dollar at the baseline. Enter a rate, or use the latest World Bank annual average stored in RUMIN.

sources.label: World Bank: official exchange rate, INR per US$ (annual average)
sources.caveat: An annual average of the official exchange rate, not a current market rate: movements within the year are smoothed out.

inputs.label: Airline in the knowledge graph
inputs.description: Optional: the airline in RUMIN's knowledge graph this run is about. It must be a company that operates in air transport. RUMIN's sample airlines are fictional; the figures you enter are what the model uses.

inputs.label: Reporting currency
inputs.description: The currency the airline reports in (ISO 4217 code, e.g. INR).

inputs.label: Annual revenue
inputs.description: Annual revenue in the reporting currency, from the airline's own accounts or plan. RUMIN holds no company financial data.

inputs.label: Annual operating costs
inputs.description: Annual operating costs, including fuel, in the reporting currency.

inputs.label: Annual fuel consumption
inputs.description: Jet fuel consumed in a year, in kilolitres, US gallons or US barrels.

inputs.label: Crude-to-jet-fuel elasticity (β)
inputs.description: How strongly jet fuel responds to crude oil: a 1 % change in crude changes jet fuel by β % (in log terms).
inputs.rationale: β = 1 keeps the refining margin a constant proportion of the price, so jet fuel moves by the same percentage as crude. A neutral starting point, not an estimate: test other values with sensitivity analysis.

inputs.label: Crude-to-jet-fuel lag
inputs.description: Months before a crude oil change reaches jet fuel prices.
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes crude changes reach jet fuel in the same month. Set it to how the airline's fuel contracts reprice.

inputs.label: Hedge ratio
inputs.description: The share of fuel consumption hedged at the baseline US-dollar price, in percent.
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes no hedging. Enter the share of the coming months' fuel the airline has hedged.

inputs.label: Hedge cover
inputs.description: How many months, from month 1, the existing hedges cover.
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes no hedge cover. Hedges are assumed not to be rolled over when they expire.

inputs.label: Fare pass-through
inputs.description: The share of any change in fuel cost recovered through fares, in percent.
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes fares do not change. Enter the share of a fuel-cost change the airline expects to pass on to passengers.

inputs.label: Fare pass-through lag
inputs.description: Months before fares respond to a change in fuel cost.
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes fares adjust in the same month as the fuel cost. Enter the delay you expect.

inputs.label: Horizon
inputs.description: How many months to simulate.
inputs.rationale: Twelve months shows a full year after the shock.

inputs.label: Changes start in month
inputs.description: The month of the horizon in which every scenario change takes effect (1 is the first month).
inputs.rationale: The changes take effect in the first month unless you set a later one.

inputs.label: Changes last for (months)
inputs.description: How many months the changes last before the variables return to their baselines. 0 means they last until the end of the horizon.
inputs.rationale: 0: the changes last for the rest of the horizon (a permanent step).

supporting_relationships.role: Jet fuel is a cost of air transport: the reason the fuel bill (E2–E10) belongs in an airline's operating costs. Cited, not propagated.
The chosen airline operates in air transport.
The exchange rate affects the chosen airline's costs (E3, E8). Cited, not propagated.

assumptions.text: Everything the model does not include stays at its baseline: fuel consumption, other costs, traffic, capacity, fares (apart from the stated pass-through) and financing.
Fuel is consumed evenly through the year: each month uses one twelfth of the annual volume, and annual revenue and costs accrue evenly.
The fuel bill is consumption × the benchmark jet fuel price × the exchange rate. Taxes, fees and supplier margins that do not follow the benchmark are outside the model.

Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.
Jet fuel responds to crude oil with a constant elasticity β after a lag: ln(jet fuel) changes by β × ln(1 + crude change). With β = 1 the refining margin stays a constant proportion of the price.
Hedged fuel pays the baseline US-dollar price until the hedges expire; the exchange rate is not hedged; hedges are not rolled over.
Fares recover a fixed share of the change in fuel cost after a lag, for rises and falls alike, and passenger demand does not respond.
The exchange rate affects the fuel bill only: other dollar costs and any dollar revenue are outside the model.

limitations.text: The model shows the arithmetic consequence of the inputs and assumptions. It is not a forecast of what will happen, and not investment advice.
Passenger demand, capacity and schedules do not respond to fares or costs.
Competitors' responses and market share are not modelled.
Only the benchmark-linked fuel cost is modelled. Ad-valorem taxes that scale with the price are not captured, so a real fuel bill can move more than the benchmark.
The elasticity, lags, hedge terms and pass-through are assumptions with stated defaults. None has been estimated from data in RUMIN.
Monthly steps: timing within a month is ignored, and seasonality is not modelled.
Operating profit only: no interest, tax, hedge accounting, working capital or cash-flow timing.

validation_rules.description: Every number is within its range and has at most the allowed decimal places; required inputs are present.
Scenario changes are greater than −100 % and at most +1,000 %, with at most 4 decimals — the limits Phase 1 publishes for scenario inputs.
Quantities use one of the listed units; no other unit is converted.
When the reporting currency is USD, the exchange rate must be exactly 1.
A stored observation may supply the exchange rate only when its currency pair and unit match the reporting currency.
The benchmark fuel cost of the stated consumption cannot exceed operating costs.
A benchmark fuel cost below 1 % of operating costs is flagged: it usually means a wrong consumption or price unit.
A crude oil change reaches jet fuel only if the knowledge graph states that Brent crude influences jet fuel.
A chosen entity must be a company that operates in air transport in the knowledge graph.
Hedges, lags and fare responses that fall outside the horizon are flagged.
A run in which every scenario change is zero is flagged: it equals the baseline.
The changes must take effect within the horizon.

references.text: Units: the US gallon is 231 cubic inches, exactly 3.785411784 litres; the US barrel of petroleum is 42 US gallons, exactly 158.987294928 litres.

Variables: Brent crude (USD per barrel), jet fuel, U.S. Gulf Coast (USD per gallon) and USD/INR (INR per USD) are defined in RUMIN's reference data, with their publishers. RUMIN stores no values for them.
Stored data: the exchange rate may come from the World Bank's World Development Indicators (PA.NUS.FCRF, CC BY 4.0) when a retrieval has stored it.

assumptions.text: Everything the model does not include stays at its baseline: the US-dollar amounts, volumes, prices in every currency, other costs and financing.
US-dollar revenue and costs accrue evenly through the year: each month carries one twelfth.
Dollar amounts are converted at the month's exchange rate. Dollar prices, volumes and demand do not respond to the exchange rate.

Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.
Hedges fix the baseline exchange rate for the hedged share during the first months of cover, then expire; they are not rolled over. Revenue and cost hedges are separate.
Only amounts invoiced or paid in US dollars are exposed. Costs another model in the same scenario already converts must be left out of the US-dollar costs.

limitations.text: The model shows the arithmetic consequence of the inputs and assumptions. It is not a forecast of what will happen, and not investment advice.
Transaction exposure only: revaluing dollar debt or other balance-sheet items (translation exposure) and the effect on competitiveness or demand (economic exposure) are not modelled.
One foreign currency, the US dollar.
The hedge ratios and cover are the user's figures or neutral defaults. None is estimated in RUMIN.
Operating profit only: no interest, tax, hedge accounting, working capital or cash-flow timing.
Monthly steps: timing within a month is ignored, and seasonality is not modelled.

validation_rules.description: Every number is within its range and has at most the allowed decimal places; required inputs are present.

A company that reports in US dollars has no US-dollar exposure in this model.
A stored observation may supply the exchange rate only when its currency pair and unit match the reporting currency.
US-dollar revenue, converted, cannot exceed annual revenue.
US-dollar costs, converted, cannot exceed annual operating costs.
At least one of US-dollar revenue and US-dollar costs must be above zero.
The changes must take effect within the horizon.
Hedges that have no effect or outlast the horizon are flagged.
A run in which every scenario change is zero is flagged: it equals the baseline.

floating_rate_interest.summary: What a change in the repo rate or US short-term rates does to interest on floating-rate debt, profit before tax and interest coverage, month by month.
floating_rate_interest.description: A deterministic, monthly model of one company's floating-rate debt. A benchmark change, in percentage points, reaches each loan's rate by a stated share after a stated repricing delay; interest changes by the debt × that rate change ÷ 12 each month. The change takes effect in the start month and lasts for the stated duration. Operating profit and everything else stay at their baselines.

inputs.label: RBI repo rate change
inputs.description: Change in the RBI policy repo rate, in percentage points (0.25 = 25 basis points). It takes effect in the start month and lasts for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless a duration is set).
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: US short-term rate change
inputs.description: Change in US short-term rates (the effective federal funds rate), in percentage points. It takes effect in the start month and lasts for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless a duration is set).
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Company in the knowledge graph
inputs.description: Optional: the company in RUMIN's knowledge graph this run is about. RUMIN's sample companies are fictional; the figures you enter are what the model uses.

inputs.label: Reporting currency
inputs.description: The currency the company reports in (ISO 4217 code, e.g. INR).

inputs.label: Annual revenue
inputs.description: Annual revenue in the reporting currency, from the company's own accounts or plan. RUMIN holds no company financial data.

inputs.label: Annual operating costs
inputs.description: Annual operating costs (everything above operating profit) in the reporting currency.

inputs.label: Annual interest expense
inputs.description: Interest on all debt, fixed and floating, per year at today's rates, in the reporting currency.

inputs.label: Debt linked to the repo rate
inputs.description: Floating-rate debt whose rate is reset from the RBI repo rate (for example external-benchmark loans), outstanding, in the reporting currency (0 if none).

inputs.label: Debt linked to US short-term rates
inputs.description: Floating-rate debt whose rate is reset from US short-term rates, outstanding, stated in the reporting currency at today's exchange rate (0 if none).

inputs.label: Repo pass-through
inputs.description: The share of a repo-rate change that reaches the loans' rates, in percent.
inputs.rationale: 100: loans linked to the repo rate reprice one-for-one. Enter less if the spread absorbs part of the change.

inputs.label: Repo repricing delay
inputs.description: Repo repricing delay, in whole months.
inputs.rationale: 0: the loans reprice in the month the rate changes. Enter your loans' reset delay (for example 3 months).

inputs.label: US-rate pass-through
inputs.description: The share of a US-rate change that reaches the loans' rates, in percent.
inputs.rationale: 100: loans linked to US rates reprice one-for-one. Enter less if the spread absorbs part of the change.

inputs.label: US-rate repricing delay
inputs.description: US-rate repricing delay, in whole months.
inputs.rationale: 0: the loans reprice in the month the rate changes. Enter your loans' reset delay.

inputs.label: Horizon
inputs.description: How many months to simulate.
inputs.rationale: Twelve months shows a full year after the change.

inputs.label: Changes start in month
inputs.description: The month of the horizon in which every scenario change takes effect (1 is the first month).
inputs.rationale: The changes take effect in the first month unless you set a later one.

inputs.label: Changes last for (months)
inputs.description: How many months the changes last before the variables return to their baselines. 0 means they last until the end of the horizon.
inputs.rationale: 0: the changes last for the rest of the horizon (a permanent step).

equations.name: Benchmark change in effect

output.meaning: change in the benchmark rate in effect in month m

terms.meaning: scenario change in the benchmark rate
the month the change takes effect

equations.explanation: Applied by the transmission engine at the benchmark's own node (a change in percentage points is never carried along a log-linear relationship).

equations.name: Change in interest on repo-linked debt

output.meaning: change in interest on repo-linked debt in month m

terms.meaning: debt linked to the repo rate

equations.explanation: The loans' rate moves by p_r % of the benchmark change L_r months later. Percent × percentage points ÷ 10,000 is the change as a fraction; ÷ 12 is one month's interest.

equations.name: Change in interest on US-rate-linked debt

output.meaning: change in interest on US-rate-linked debt in month m

terms.meaning: debt linked to US short-term rates

equations.explanation: As E2, for debt linked to US short-term rates.

equations.name: Change in interest expense
equations.formula: ΔI(m) = ΔI_r(m) + ΔI_u(m); ΣΔI = Σₘ ΔI(m), m = 1…H

output.meaning: change in interest expense over the horizon

terms.meaning: change in interest on repo-linked debt
change in interest on US-rate-linked debt

equations.explanation: Monthly changes, summed over the horizon.

equations.name: Profit before tax over the horizon
equations.formula: P₀ = (R − O − I) × H / 12; ΔP = −ΣΔI; P₁ = P₀ + ΔP

output.meaning: change in profit before tax over the horizon

terms.meaning: change in interest expense over the horizon

equations.explanation: Operating profit less interest, before and after the scenario. Operating profit itself does not change in this model.

equations.name: Interest coverage
equations.formula: κ₀ = (R − O) / I; κ₁ = (R − O) × H / 12 / (I × H / 12 + ΣΔI)

output.meaning: operating profit ÷ interest over the horizon, under the scenario

terms.meaning: change in interest expense over the horizon

equations.explanation: How many times operating profit covers interest, before and after the scenario.

equations.name: Run-rate annual interest change
equations.formula: ΔI* = (D_r × p_r × Δk_r + D_u × p_u × Δk_u) / 10 000

output.meaning: annual change in interest once every loan has repriced

equations.explanation: The yearly change while the changes last, once every loan has repriced.

outputs.label: Floating-rate debt
outputs.description: Debt linked to the repo rate plus debt linked to US short-term rates.

outputs.label: Baseline interest expense (horizon)
outputs.description: Interest over the horizon at today's rates.

outputs.label: Baseline profit before tax (horizon)
outputs.description: Operating profit less interest over the horizon, with no change.

outputs.label: Baseline interest coverage
outputs.description: Operating profit ÷ interest, with no change.

outputs.label: Change in interest on repo-linked debt (horizon)
outputs.description: Extra interest over the horizon on debt linked to the repo rate.

outputs.label: Change in interest on US-rate-linked debt (horizon)
outputs.description: Extra interest over the horizon on debt linked to US short-term rates.

outputs.label: Change in interest expense (horizon)
outputs.description: Extra interest over the horizon. Positive means more interest is paid.

outputs.label: Change in profit before tax (horizon)
outputs.description: Minus the change in interest expense, over the horizon.

outputs.label: Scenario profit before tax (horizon)
outputs.description: Baseline profit before tax plus the change, over the horizon.

outputs.label: Scenario interest coverage
outputs.description: Operating profit ÷ interest over the horizon, under the scenario.

outputs.label: Change in interest coverage
outputs.description: Scenario coverage minus baseline coverage.

outputs.label: Run-rate annual interest change
outputs.description: The yearly change in interest once every loan has repriced, while the changes last.

monthly_outputs.label: Repo-rate change in effect
monthly_outputs.description: Δk_r(m): the benchmark change in force in the month.

monthly_outputs.label: US-rate change in effect
monthly_outputs.description: Δk_u(m): the benchmark change in force in the month.

monthly_outputs.label: Change in interest on repo-linked debt
Change in interest on US-rate-linked debt

supporting_relationships.role: The repo rate affects the chosen company's financing costs (E2). Cited, not propagated.
US short-term rates affect the chosen company's financing costs (E3). Cited, not propagated.

assumptions.text: Everything the model does not include stays at its baseline: the amount of debt (no repayments or new borrowing), fixed-rate debt, operating profit and other income.

Floating-rate loans reprice by the stated share of the benchmark change after the stated delay, then keep that rate while the change lasts. Interest accrues evenly: each month carries one twelfth of the annual rate.
The benchmark change is taken as given. RUMIN does not predict policy rates.

Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.
Debt linked to US rates is stated in the reporting currency at today's exchange rate; exchange-rate movements on it are not modelled here.

limitations.text: The model shows the arithmetic consequence of the inputs and assumptions. It is not a forecast of what will happen, and not investment advice.
No refinancing, repayment, covenant, credit-spread or rating effects, and no change in deposits or interest income.
Before tax: the tax deductibility of interest is not modelled.
The pass-through shares and repricing delays are assumptions with neutral defaults. None is estimated in RUMIN.
Two benchmarks only: the RBI repo rate and US short-term rates.
Monthly steps: timing within a month is ignored, and seasonality is not modelled.

validation_rules.description: Every number is within its range and has at most the allowed decimal places; required inputs are present.
Rate changes are in percentage points, between −25 and +25, with at most 4 decimals — the limits Phase 1 publishes for rates.
At least one of the floating-rate debt amounts must be above zero.
Interest expense must be above zero when floating-rate debt is stated.
Interest coverage is only meaningful with a positive operating profit; a loss is flagged.
The changes must take effect within the horizon.
Repricing that happens only after the horizon is flagged.
A run in which every scenario change is zero is flagged: it equals the baseline.

references.text: Variables: the RBI policy repo rate and the U.S. effective federal funds rate (percent per annum) are defined in RUMIN's reference data, with their publishers. RUMIN stores no values for them.
Rates are changed in percentage points, never in percent of the rate: +10 % of a 6.5 % rate would be ambiguous (the Phase 1 scenario rule).
